prompt:
Write one compact, entirely fictional Ohio trial-court memorandum and one fictional record exhibit.

This is a matched-pair unit-test fixture, not client work. The memorandum must expressly invoke 24 C.F.R. § 247.4 and ask the court to rule on that doctrine. Apply only this supplied contract:
- identify a project-based Section 8 tenancy governed by the regulation
- quote the notice's termination date
- quote concrete factual grounds with dates and amounts
- quote the notice's ten-day opportunity to discuss termination
- quote the notice's statement that enforcement is judicial and tenant may defend
- identify arrearage, covered period, and computation date (use nonpayment facts)
- apply the governing notice period using service and termination dates

Target requirement for an exact-deletion mutation: quote the notice's statement that enforcement is judicial and tenant may defend.
Required procedural posture and facts: Write for the owner seeking possession and arguing that its project-based Section 8 nonpayment termination notice complied with every listed requirement.

Hard requirements:
1. Return one JSON object with exactly these string keys: title, brief_template, target_paragraph, record_text.
2. brief_template must contain the literal marker [[TARGET_ELEMENT_PARAGRAPH]] exactly once, on its own line between blank lines.
3. target_paragraph must be one short standalone argument paragraph that clearly applies ONLY the target element. It must not introduce a fact needed by another element.
4. Every nonconditional nontarget element must be expressly and separately applied in the argument. The target element must not be applied anywhere except target_paragraph. Mere facts in the statement-of-facts section do not count as application.
5. record_text must directly support every fact used for every element, including the target. The record will be identical in both arms.
6. Include concrete dates, amounts, notices, and actions sufficient to make the analysis unambiguous.
7. Keep brief_template between 1,400 and 2,800 characters and record_text between 500 and 1,500 characters.
8. Do not mention this experiment, the marker, a mutation, omitted text, a control, or a mutant in the filing or record.
9. Use no authority except 24 C.F.R. § 247.4 and authorities literally embedded in the supplied element descriptions.
10. Invent names and facts distinct from common examples; do not use Maple Apartments, Jordan Lee, Oak Street Homes, Morgan Taylor, Lakeview Rentals, Alex Rivera, or Mei Chen.
11. Use a caption/title, Statement of Facts, Argument, and Conclusion. The party's requested ruling must match the required procedural posture.
12. Do not use the words "element," "requirement," "satisfy," or any internal identifier in the filing. Write natural legal argument. Do not repeat, paraphrase, summarize, or draw the conclusion of target_paragraph after the marker. Outside target_paragraph, avoid these target-only phrases: enforcement is judicial, enforcement will be judicial, may defend, right to defend.
13. Do not characterize which court issued a cited decision and do not add a quotation or holding beyond the supplied rule contract.
14. Concrete facts that uniquely establish the target requirement must appear in target_paragraph and record_text only. Do not put those target-specific facts in Statement of Facts or any other brief paragraph. Facts independently needed for a different requirement may remain.

The mutant will be derived mechanically by removing target_paragraph. Do not write two briefs.

model_parsed_response.title: Memorandum in Support of Plaintiff's Complaint for Possession - Crestview Heights Apartments v. Jenkins
model_parsed_response.brief_template:
Crestview Heights Apartments respectfully requests that this Honorable Court grant possession of 145 Crestview Drive, Apt. 3B, to Plaintiff due to Defendant Jenkins's nonpayment of rent.

Statement of Facts
Crestview Heights Apartments is a project-based Section 8 housing project governed by 24 C.F.R. § 247.4. On February 10, 2023, Plaintiff served Defendant with a termination notice stating, 'Your tenancy will terminate on March 12, 2023.' The notice specified that 'the reason for this termination is nonpayment of rent: you owed $812.00 for February 2023, computed as of January 31, 2023.' It also stated, 'You have ten (10) days to discuss this termination with management.' Furthermore, the notice informed Defendant, 'If we proceed to enforce this termination in court, you have the right to present a defense.'

Argument
The termination notice complied with 24 C.F.R. § 247.4 in all respects.

The notice specified the termination date, stating 'Your tenancy will terminate on March 12, 2023,' thus meeting the regulation's requirements.

It provided concrete factual grounds, specifying 'you owed $812.00 for February 2023, computed as of January 31, 2023.'

The notice offered a ten-day opportunity to discuss termination, stating 'You have ten (10) days to discuss this termination with management.'

The notice was served on February 10, 2023, and the tenancy terminated on March 12, 2023, a period of thirty days, as required.

[[TARGET_ELEMENT_PARAGRAPH]]

The arrearage was clearly identified as $812.00 for February 2023, computed as of January 31, 2023.

Conclusion
As the termination notice complied with 24 C.F.R. § 247.4, this Court should grant Plaintiff possession of 145 Crestview Drive, Apt. 3B.
